title: Ξεινήια καὶ λοετρά
titleEn: The Guest-Gifts and the Bath — Odyssey 8.387–486
source: Homer, The Odyssey, Greek text of A. T. Murray (Loeb Classical Library; London: Heinemann, New York: Putnam, 1919), public domain; TEI from PerseusDL/canonical-greekLit tlg0012.tlg002.perseus-grc2, sha256 7d7ffafb6c51f8c2. Text as printed: Murray sets no quotation marks round speeches, and none are added. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca — an admitted convention; Homer's own pronunciation was older and is not recoverable in detail. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; ï for a separately sounded ι; accents omitted). Scansion: made by program from the text and checked; it shows one defensible reading of each line, and the notes say where a line is irregular. All translations were made fresh from the Greek for Lectorium.
about: Alcinous, speaking to the Phaeacian leaders, proposes that each of the twelve kings under him give the stranger a cloak, a tunic and a talent of gold, and that Euryalus, whose word to the guest was out of measure, make amends. Euryalus gives a bronze sword with a silver hilt and an ivory sheath, and Odysseus answers with a wish for his good fortune. At the palace the gifts are carried in and Arete packs them in a chest, Alcinous adds his own golden cup, and the maids heat water for a bath. Arete tells Odysseus to secure the chest, and he does so with the knot Circe once taught him. After a bath such as he has not had since leaving Calypso, and dressed in fine clothes, he meets Nausicaa at the doorway: she asks him to remember her, and he answers that he will pray to her as to a god, because she gave him life. At the feast he sends Demodocus a cut from the chine of a white-toothed pig, saying that minstrels deserve honour because the Muse taught them, and the part closes as he begins to speak to the minstrel.

sentences.t: κέκλυτε, Φαιήκων ἡγήτορες ἠδὲ μέδοντες.
sentences.tr: keklyte, Phaiēkōn hēgētores ēde medontes.
sentences.l: “Hear me, leaders and lords of the Phaeacians.
sentences.i: “Hear me, leaders and lords of the Phaeacians.
sentences.n: κέκλυτε is the aorist imperative of κλύω 'hear, listen', in its reduplicated epic shape, the call that opens a speech before a company. Φαιήκων ἡγήτορες ἠδὲ μέδοντες is 'leaders and lords of the Phaeacians': Φαιήκων is a genitive plural, ἠδέ is epic 'and', and μέδοντες is a participle of μέδω 'rule over', used as a noun. This is Alcinous speaking: the speech introduced by μετηύδα at the close of the previous part begins with these words, so the opening quotation mark and the speaker's label above the line fall on this first unit.

sentences.t: ὁ ξεῖνος μάλα μοι δοκέει πεπνυμένος εἶναι.
sentences.tr: ho xeinos mala moi dokeei pepnymenos einai.
sentences.l: The stranger greatly to me seems prudent to be.
sentences.i: The stranger seems to me to be very prudent.
sentences.n: ὁ ξεῖνος 'the stranger': in Homer ὁ is still close to a pronoun, 'this one, the stranger'. δοκέει is the uncontracted form of δοκεῖ 'seems', with μοι 'to me'. πεπνυμένος is the perfect participle of a verb for having one's wits about one (πέπνυμαι, related to πνέω 'breathe'); it is kept as 'prudent' wherever it is used, and εἶναι completes δοκέει, 'seems to be prudent'.

sentences.t: ἀλλ’ ἄγε οἱ δῶμεν ξεινήιον, ὡς ἐπιεικές.
sentences.tr: all’ age hoi dōmen xeinēion, hōs epieikes.
sentences.l: But come, to him let us give a guest-gift, as is fitting.
sentences.i: But come, let us give him a guest-gift, as is fitting.
sentences.n: ἀλλ’ ἄγε 'but come now'. δῶμεν is an aorist subjunctive of δίδωμι in the exhortation 'let us give'. οἱ is 'to him' (the dative of the pronoun ἕ), not the relative. ξεινήιον 'guest-gift': the present a host gives a guest, Ionic for Attic ξένιον. ὡς ἐπιεικές 'as is fitting', with 'it is' understood.

sentences.t:
δώδεκα γὰρ κατὰ δῆμον ἀριπρεπέες βασιλῆες
ἀρχοὶ κραίνουσι, τρισκαιδέκατος δ’ ἐγὼ αὐτός·
sentences.tr:
dōdeka gar kata dēmon ariprepees basilēes
archoi krainousi, triskaidekatos d’ egō autos·
sentences.l:
For twelve throughout the land outstanding kings
as chiefs hold sway, and thirteenth, I myself;
sentences.i: For twelve outstanding kings hold sway as chiefs throughout the land, and I myself am the thirteenth;
sentences.n: δώδεκα γάρ 'for twelve' begins the reason for a gift from many hands. κατὰ δῆμον 'throughout the land' (δῆμος, here the country and its people). βασιλῆες 'kings' are the twelve nobles who rule under Alcinous. ἀριπρεπέες is an uncontracted nominative plural of ἀριπρεπής 'outstanding' (ἀρι- is an intensifying prefix). ἀρχοί 'chiefs' stands beside it as an apposition, 'as rulers'. κραίνουσι 'they hold sway'. τρισκαιδέκατος 'thirteenth' with ἐγὼ αὐτός 'I myself': Alcinous counts himself the thirteenth.

sentences.t:
τῶν οἱ ἕκαστος φᾶρος ἐυπλυνὲς ἠδὲ χιτῶνα
καὶ χρυσοῖο τάλαντον ἐνείκατε τιμήεντος.
sentences.tr:
tōn hoi hekastos pharos eyplynes ēde chitōna
kai chrysoio talanton eneikate timēentos.
sentences.l:
Of these, for him each a well-washed cloak and a tunic
and a talent of precious gold bring.
sentences.i: Let each of them bring him a well-washed cloak and a tunic and a talent of precious gold.
sentences.n: τῶν οἱ ἕκαστος: τῶν is the genitive plural 'of them' (the twelve kings, named just above), οἱ is 'for him' (the guest), and ἕκαστος is 'each one'. The verb ἐνείκατε is a plural imperative (aorist of φέρω; Attic ἐνέγκατε), so the sentence begins with a singular 'each' and ends with a plural command, which Greek allows. φᾶρος is a cloak (here a man's outer garment), ἐυπλυνές 'well-washed' (printed without a diaeresis over the υ), χιτών 'tunic', τάλαντον 'a talent', a fixed weight of gold. τιμήεντος is a genitive, 'of precious (gold)'.

sentences.t:
αἶψα δὲ πάντα φέρωμεν ἀολλέα, ὄφρ’ ἐνὶ χερσὶν
ξεῖνος ἔχων ἐπὶ δόρπον ἴῃ χαίρων ἐνὶ θυμῷ.
sentences.tr:
aipsa de panta pherōmen aollea, ophr’ eni chersin
xeinos echōn epi dorpon iēi chairōn eni thymōi.
sentences.l:
And at once let us bring all of it together, so that in his hands
the stranger, holding it, may go to supper rejoicing in his heart.
sentences.i: And let us bring it all together at once, so that the stranger may go to supper holding it in his hands, rejoicing in his heart.
sentences.n: φέρωμεν is a subjunctive of exhortation, 'let us bring'. ἀολλέα 'in a body, all together' agrees with πάντα 'everything'. ὄφρα 'so that' takes the subjunctive ἴῃ (from εἶμι 'go'): 'that he may go'. ἐνὶ χερσίν: ἐνί is ἐν, and χερσίν a dative plural, 'in his hands'; ἔχων 'holding' has the gifts as its unstated object. ἐπὶ δόρπον 'to supper': ἐπί with the accusative gives the goal. χαίρων ἐνὶ θυμῷ 'rejoicing in his heart'; θυμός is 'heart' in the house renderings.

sentences.t:
Εὐρύαλος δέ ἑ αὐτὸν ἀρεσσάσθω ἐπέεσσι
καὶ δώρῳ, ἐπεὶ οὔ τι ἔπος κατὰ μοῖραν ἔειπεν.
sentences.tr:
Euryalos de he auton aressasthō epeessi
kai dōrōi, epei ou ti epos kata moiran eeipen.
sentences.l:
And Euryalus him himself let appease with words
and with a gift, since not at all a word according to what is fitting he spoke.”
sentences.i: And let Euryalus himself make amends to him with words and with a gift, since he did not speak a word as is fitting.”
sentences.n: ἀρεσσάσθω is a third-person aorist imperative middle of ἀρέσκω 'please, appease', so 'let him appease, make amends to'. ἑ is 'him' and αὐτόν 'himself' in apposition: 'him himself'. ἐπέεσσι is an uncontracted dative plural 'with words'; δώρῳ 'with a gift'. ἔειπεν is the aorist of the verb 'say', in a lengthened epic form (Attic εἶπεν). κατὰ μοῖραν 'as is fitting' (literally 'according to due measure'). Alcinous' speech ends with this unit; the point is that Euryalus' word to the guest was out of measure, and it is Euryalus who is to put it right.

sentences.t:
ὣς ἔφαθ’, οἱ δ’ ἄρα πάντες ἐπῄνεον ἠδ’ ἐκέλευον,
δῶρα δ’ ἄρ’ οἰσέμεναι πρόεσαν κήρυκα ἕκαστος.
sentences.tr:
hōs ephath’, hoi d’ ara pantes epēineon ēd’ ekeleuon,
dōra d’ ar’ oisemenai proesan kēryka hekastos.
sentences.l:
So he spoke, and they then all praised it and urged him on,
and gifts to bring they sent a herald, each one.
sentences.i: So he spoke, and they all applauded and urged him on, and each one sent a herald off to fetch gifts.
sentences.n: ὣς ἔφαθ’ 'So he spoke': ἔφαθ’ is ἔφατο with its last vowel elided and the τ made rough by the rough breathing of οἱ that follows. ἐπῄνεον 'they praised, approved' and ἐκέλευον 'they urged' are imperfects. οἰσέμεναι is an infinitive of purpose, 'to bring' (from the future stem οἰσ- of φέρω, with the epic ending -έμεναι). πρόεσαν 'they sent forth' (aorist of προΐημι); κήρυκα ἕκαστος is a singular, 'each a herald'. This line stands word for word in another passage, and its English is kept.

sentences.t: τὸν δ’ αὖτ’ Εὐρύαλος ἀπαμείβετο φώνησέν τε·
sentences.tr: ton d’ aut’ Euryalos apameibeto phōnēsen te·
sentences.l: Him then in turn answered Euryalus, and spoke:
sentences.i: Then Euryalus answered him in turn, and spoke:
sentences.n: The reply-formula: τὸν is the pronoun 'him', not the article; αὖτ’ is αὖτε 'in turn'. ἀπαμείβετο 'answered' is an imperfect middle, and φώνησεν 'spoke, uttered' an aorist, joined by -τε 'and'. Euryalus is the man whose word Alcinous has just called out of measure; his speech begins in the next unit. The line stands unchanged elsewhere, and its English is kept.

sentences.t:
Ἀλκίνοε κρεῖον, πάντων ἀριδείκετε λαῶν,
τοιγὰρ ἐγὼ τὸν ξεῖνον ἀρέσσομαι, ὡς σὺ κελεύεις.
sentences.tr:
Alkinoe kreion, pantōn arideikete laōn,
toigar egō ton xeinon aressomai, hōs sy keleueis.
sentences.l:
“Alcinous, lord, most conspicuous of all the people,
therefore I the stranger will appease, as you bid.
sentences.i: “Alcinous, my lord, most distinguished of all the people, therefore I will make amends to the stranger, as you bid.
sentences.n: Ἀλκίνοε, κρεῖον and ἀριδείκετε are vocatives: κρείων 'lord, ruler', and ἀριδείκετος, whose sense is 'most conspicuous' (the first part is an intensifier, as in ἀριπρεπής). πάντων ... λαῶν 'of all the people' (λαῶν is the genitive plural of λαός). τοιγάρ 'therefore, well then'. ἀρέσσομαι is the future of ἀρέσκω, 'I will appease, make amends to', the same verb Alcinous used at 396. ὡς σὺ κελεύεις 'as you bid'. Euryalus begins to speak here, so the quotation mark opens and the note above the line names him.

sentences.t:
δώσω οἱ τόδ’ ἄορ παγχάλκεον, ᾧ ἔπι κώπη
ἀργυρέη, κολεὸν δὲ νεοπρίστου ἐλέφαντος
ἀμφιδεδίνηται·
sentences.tr:
dōsō hoi tod’ aor panchalkeon, hōi epi kōpē
argyreē, koleon de neopristou elephantos
amphidedinētai·
sentences.i: I will give him this sword, all of bronze, on which there is a hilt of silver, while a sheath of newly sawn ivory has been set round it;
sentences.n: δώσω is the future 'I will give', with οἱ 'to him'. ἄορ 'sword' is the poetic word, and παγχάλκεον 'all of bronze'. ᾧ ἔπι: ᾧ 'on which' is a relative, and ἔπι is ἐπί with its accent thrown back because it follows the relative it governs. κώπη ἀργυρέη 'a hilt of silver' has no verb of its own, 'on which (is) a silver hilt'. κολεόν 'sheath'; νεοπρίστου ἐλέφαντος 'of newly sawn ivory' (πρίω 'saw'). ἀμφιδεδίνηται is a perfect passive of ἀμφιδινέω 'whirl round, set round', with the sheath as subject.

sentences.t: πολέος δέ οἱ ἄξιον ἔσται.
sentences.tr: poleos de hoi axion estai.
sentences.l: and of much worth to him it will be.”
sentences.i: and it will be worth much to him.”
sentences.n: πολέος is a genitive of price (Attic πολλοῦ), 'of much', with ἄξιον 'worth': the sword will be worth a great deal to him. οἱ 'to him'. The speech ends with this unit.

sentences.t:
ὣς εἰπὼν ἐν χερσὶ τίθει ξίφος ἀργυρόηλον
καί μιν φωνήσας ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα·
sentences.tr:
hōs eipōn en chersi tithei xiphos argyroēlon
kai min phōnēsas epea pteroenta prosēuda·
sentences.l:
So having spoken, in his hands he placed the silver-studded sword,
and, lifting his voice, to him winged words he spoke:
sentences.i: With these words he placed the silver-studded sword in his hands, and lifting his voice he spoke winged words to him:
sentences.n: ὣς εἰπών 'so having spoken'. ἐν χερσὶ τίθει 'in his hands he placed': τίθει is an imperfect without the augment (Attic ἐτίθει). ξίφος ἀργυρόηλον 'a silver-studded sword' (ἀργυρόηλος 'with silver studs or nails'). The second line is the stock speech-opener: μιν 'him', φωνήσας 'having lifted his voice', ἔπεα πτερόεντα 'winged words', προσηύδα 'he spoke to'. The line stands elsewhere word for word, and its English is kept.

sentences.t: χαῖρε, πάτερ ὦ ξεῖνε·
sentences.tr: chaire, pater ō xeine·
sentences.l: “Welcome, father, O stranger;
sentences.i: “Welcome, stranger, my father;
sentences.n: χαῖρε is the imperative of χαίρω, here the greeting 'welcome'. πάτερ 'father' is a courteous form of address to an older man, and claims no kinship; ὦ ξεῖνε 'O stranger'. Euryalus begins to speak to Odysseus here, so the quotation mark opens and the note above the line names him.

sentences.t:
ἔπος δ’ εἴ πέρ τι βέβακται
δεινόν, ἄφαρ τὸ φέροιεν ἀναρπάξασαι ἄελλαι.
sentences.tr:
epos d’ ei per ti bebaktai
deinon, aphar to pheroien anarpaxasai aellai.
sentences.l:
and if indeed any word has been spoken
terrible, at once that may carry off, snatching it up, the storm-blasts.
sentences.i: and if any terrible word has been spoken, may the storm-blasts snatch it up and carry it off at once.
sentences.n: ἔπος δ’ εἴ πέρ τι βέβακται 'and if indeed any word has been spoken': εἴ πέρ 'if indeed', and βέβακται is a perfect passive of βάζω 'speak', so 'has been spoken'. δεινόν 'terrible'. ἄφαρ 'at once'; τὸ 'it'. φέροιεν is an optative of wish, 'may they carry off', with ἀναρπάξασαι 'snatching up' (aorist participle, feminine plural) agreeing with ἄελλαι 'storm-blasts', the subject.

sentences.t:
σοὶ δὲ θεοὶ ἄλοχόν τ’ ἰδέειν καὶ πατρίδ’ ἱκέσθαι
δοῖεν, ἐπεὶ δὴ δηθὰ φίλων ἄπο πήματα πάσχεις.
sentences.tr:
soi de theoi alochon t’ ideein kai patrid’ hikesthai
doien, epei dē dētha philōn apo pēmata pascheis.
sentences.l:
And to you may the gods grant both to see your wife and to reach your fatherland,
since indeed for a long time far from your dear ones woes you suffer.”
sentences.i: And may the gods grant you to see your wife and reach your fatherland, since you have long been suffering woes far from your dear ones.”
sentences.n: σοί 'to you'. δοῖεν is an aorist optative of δίδωμι, 'may they grant', and governs the two infinitives ἰδέειν (the uncontracted aorist infinitive of the verb 'see'; Attic ἰδεῖν) and ἱκέσθαι 'to reach'. ἄλοχον 'wife'; πατρίδ’ is the elided accusative 'fatherland'. ἐπεὶ δή 'since indeed'. δηθά 'for a long time'. φίλων ἄπο 'far from your dear ones': ἄπο stands after its noun, and φίλων is a genitive plural 'dear ones' (family and friends). πήματα 'woes'. The speech ends with this unit.

sentences.t: τὸν δ’ ἀπαμειβόμενος προσέφη πολύμητις Ὀδυσσεύς·
sentences.tr: ton d’ apameibomenos prosephē polymētis Odysseus·
sentences.l: Him answering addressed many-wiled Odysseus:
sentences.i: In answer Odysseus of many wiles said to him:
sentences.n: The reply-formula: τὸν is the pronoun 'him'. ἀπαμειβόμενος 'answering' is a participle, and προσέφη 'addressed' an aorist of the verb 'say to'. πολύμητις 'of many wiles': μῆτις is cunning intelligence, craft. The line stands unchanged elsewhere, and its English is kept.

sentences.t: καὶ σὺ φίλος μάλα χαῖρε, θεοὶ δέ τοι ὄλβια δοῖεν.
sentences.tr: kai sy philos mala chaire, theoi de toi olbia doien.
sentences.l: “And you also, friend, very much welcome, and to you the gods blessings may give.
sentences.i: “And you too, friend, a hearty welcome; and may the gods give you blessings.
sentences.n: καὶ σὺ φίλος 'you too, friend': φίλος is a nominative used as a vocative. μάλα χαῖρε 'very much welcome', answering the greeting just given. τοι 'to you'. ὄλβια is a neuter plural of ὄλβιος 'blessed, prosperous' used as a noun, 'blessings'. δοῖεν is the optative of wish as before. Odysseus answers here, so the quotation mark opens and the note above the line names him.

sentences.t:
μηδέ τι τοι ξίφεός γε ποθὴ μετόπισθε γένοιτο
τούτου, ὃ δή μοι δῶκας ἀρεσσάμενος ἐπέεσσιν.
sentences.tr:
mēde ti toi xipheos ge pothē metopisthe genoito
toutou, ho dē moi dōkas aressamenos epeessin.
sentences.l:
And may not any longing for the sword hereafter come to you,
for this one, which you gave me, having appeased me with words.”
sentences.i: And may you never afterwards feel the want of this sword, which you gave me when you made amends with your words.”
sentences.n: μηδέ ... γένοιτο is a wish: 'and let there not come'. τοι 'to you'; ποθή 'longing, a sense of want'; μετόπισθε 'afterwards'. ξίφεος is the uncontracted genitive of ξίφος (Attic ξίφους), and τούτου 'of this one' agrees with it. ὅ 'which' is a relative; δῶκας 'you gave' (aorist). ἀρεσσάμενος 'having appeased (me)' echoes ἀρεσσάσθω at 396 and ἀρέσσομαι at 402. ἐπέεσσιν 'with words'. The speech ends with this unit.

sentences.t: ἦ ῥα καὶ ἀμφ’ ὤμοισι θέτο ξίφος ἀργυρόηλον.
sentences.tr: ē rha kai amph’ ōmoisi theto xiphos argyroēlon.
sentences.l: He spoke, and about his shoulders he put the silver-studded sword.
sentences.i: So he said, and put the silver-studded sword about his shoulders.
sentences.n: ἦ ῥα καί: ἦ is a fixed form of the verb 'say' (ἠμί), so 'he spoke', ῥα is a particle 'then', and καί 'and'; the phrase closes a speech. ἀμφ’ ὤμοισι 'about his shoulders' (a dative plural in -οισι). θέτο is an aorist middle without the augment, 'he put on himself'. ξίφος ἀργυρόηλον 'the silver-studded sword', the same as at 406.

sentences.t: δύσετό τ’ ἠέλιος, καὶ τῷ κλυτὰ δῶρα παρῆεν.
sentences.tr: dyseto t’ ēelios, kai tōi klyta dōra parēen.
sentences.l: And the sun set, and for him famous gifts were at hand.
sentences.i: The sun set, and the famous gifts were at hand for him.
sentences.n: δύσετο is an aorist middle without the augment, 'it sank, set'. ἠέλιος is the Ionic form of ἥλιος 'sun'. τῷ 'for him' (a pronoun in the dative). κλυτά 'famous' is the stock word for anything renowned. παρῆεν is the imperfect of πάρειμι 'be at hand' (Attic παρῆν).

sentences.t: καὶ τά γ’ ἐς Ἀλκινόοιο φέρον κήρυκες ἀγαυοί·
sentences.tr: kai ta g’ es Alkinooio pheron kērykes agauoi·
sentences.l: And these to Alcinous’ house carried the noble heralds;
sentences.i: And the noble heralds carried these to the house of Alcinous;
sentences.n: τά γε 'these' (the gifts): τά is a pronoun. ἐς Ἀλκινόοιο is 'to (the house) of Alcinous', with 'house' understood after a genitive in -οιο (Attic -ου). φέρον 'carried' (imperfect, without the augment). ἀγαυοί is a stock epithet meaning 'noble', kept as 'noble' every time.

sentences.t:
δεξάμενοι δ’ ἄρα παῖδες ἀμύμονος Ἀλκινόοιο
μητρὶ παρ’ αἰδοίῃ ἔθεσαν περικαλλέα δῶρα.
sentences.tr:
dexamenoi d’ ara paides amymonos Alkinooio
mētri par’ aidoiēi ethesan perikallea dōra.
sentences.l:
and having received them, the sons of blameless Alcinous
beside their revered mother placed the very fair gifts.
sentences.i: and the sons of blameless Alcinous received them and set the very fair gifts beside their revered mother.
sentences.n: δεξάμενοι is an aorist middle participle, 'having received'. παῖδες ἀμύμονος Ἀλκινόοιο 'the sons of blameless Alcinous': the sense of ἀμύμων is not really known, and 'blameless' is the traditional guess, kept every time even when it sits oddly. μητρὶ παρ’ αἰδοίῃ 'beside their revered mother' (μητρί is a dative; αἰδοίῃ 'revered'); she is named Arete at 423. ἔθεσαν 'they placed' (aorist of τίθημι). περικαλλέα 'very fair' (περι- is an intensifier on κάλλος 'beauty').

sentences.t:
τοῖσιν δ’ ἡγεμόνευ’ ἱερὸν μένος Ἀλκινόοιο,
ἐλθόντες δὲ καθῖζον ἐν ὑψηλοῖσι θρόνοισι.
sentences.tr:
toisin d’ hēgemoneu’ hieron menos Alkinooio,
elthontes de kathizon en hypsēloisi thronoisi.
sentences.l:
And for them led the way the sacred strength of Alcinous,
and having come they sat down on high chairs.
sentences.i: The sacred strength of Alcinous led the way for them, and when they had come they took their seats on high chairs.
sentences.n: τοῖσιν 'for them' is a pronoun in the dative plural. ἡγεμόνευ’ is ἡγεμόνευε, 'he led the way' (imperfect). ἱερὸν μένος Ἀλκινόοιο 'the sacred strength of Alcinous' is a periphrasis: the king is named through his strength, not by his bare name. ἐλθόντες 'having come'. καθῖζον 'they took their seats' (imperfect of καθίζω, 'were sitting down'). ὑψηλοῖσι θρόνοισι is a dative plural, 'on high chairs'.

sentences.t: δή ῥα τότ’ Ἀρήτην προσέφη μένος Ἀλκινόοιο·
sentences.tr: dē rha tot’ Arētēn prosephē menos Alkinooio·
sentences.l: Then indeed to Arete addressed the strength of Alcinous:
sentences.i: Then the strength of Alcinous said to Arete:
sentences.n: δή ῥα τότε 'then indeed': the particles δή and ῥα and the adverb τότε 'then' mark the next step. Ἀρήτην is the accusative object of προσέφη 'addressed', and Alcinous is the subject, named by the periphrasis μένος Ἀλκινόοιο 'the strength of Alcinous'. Arete is his wife, and this is the first time in this part that she is spoken to. His words follow in the next unit.

sentences.t: δεῦρο, γύναι, φέρε χηλὸν ἀριπρεπέ’, ἥ τις ἀρίστη·
sentences.tr: deuro, gynai, phere chēlon ariprepe’, hē tis aristē·
sentences.l: “Come here, wife, bring a chest, outstanding, whichever is best;
sentences.i: “Come here, wife, bring a chest, an outstanding one, whichever is best;
sentences.n: δεῦρο 'come here'. γύναι is the vocative of γυνή; a husband speaking to his wife, so 'wife'. φέρε 'bring' (imperative). χηλόν 'a chest'. ἀριπρεπέ’ is the elided accusative of ἀριπρεπής 'outstanding'. ἥ τις ἀρίστη 'whichever is best': ἥ is the relative here (feminine, agreeing with the chest), with τις making it 'whichever'. Alcinous begins a new speech, this time to Arete, so the quotation mark opens and the note above the line names him.

sentences.t: ἐν δ’ αὐτὴ θὲς φᾶρος ἐυπλυνὲς ἠδὲ χιτῶνα.
sentences.tr: en d’ autē thes pharos eyplynes ēde chitōna.
sentences.l: and in it yourself put a well-washed cloak and a tunic.
sentences.i: and put in it, yourself, a well-washed cloak and a tunic.
sentences.n: ἐν 'in it' is an adverb; θές is the short aorist imperative of τίθημι, 'put'. αὐτή 'yourself': Arete is to pack the clothes with her own hands. φᾶρος ἐυπλυνὲς ἠδὲ χιτῶνα is the very phrase Alcinous used at 392, and the English is kept.

sentences.t:
ἀμφὶ δέ οἱ πυρὶ χαλκὸν ἰήνατε, θέρμετε δ’ ὕδωρ,
ὄφρα λοεσσάμενός τε ἰδών τ’ ἐὺ κείμενα πάντα
δῶρα, τά οἱ Φαίηκες ἀμύμονες ἐνθάδ’ ἔνεικαν,
δαιτί τε τέρπηται καὶ ἀοιδῆς ὕμνον ἀκούων.
sentences.tr:
amphi de hoi pyri chalkon iēnate, thermete d’ hydōr,
ophra loessamenos te idōn t’ ey keimena panta
dōra, ta hoi Phaiēkes amymones enthad’ eneikan,
daiti te terpētai kai aoidēs hymnon akouōn.
sentences.l:
And around the fire, for him, warm the bronze, and heat the water,
so that having bathed and having seen well laid
all the gifts, which the blameless Phaeacians brought here for him,
he may take pleasure in the feast and in hearing the strain of song.
sentences.i: And about the fire warm the bronze cauldron for him, and heat water, so that, after he has bathed and seen all the gifts lying in good order, which the blameless Phaeacians brought here for him, he may take pleasure in the feast and in hearing the strain of song.
sentences.n: ἰήνατε and θέρμετε are plural imperatives, 'warm' and 'heat', spoken to the household women. ἀμφὶ ... πυρί 'about the fire' (the adverb ἀμφί goes with the dative πυρί); χαλκόν 'bronze' stands for the bronze vessel, the cauldron. οἱ 'for him'. ὄφρα 'so that' takes the subjunctive τέρπηται 'he may take pleasure', with two participles: λοεσσάμενος 'having bathed' (aorist middle) and ἰδών 'having seen'. ἐὺ κείμενα 'well laid' agrees with πάντα δῶρα 'all the gifts'. τά οἱ Φαίηκες ἀμύμονες ἐνθάδ’ ἔνεικαν 'which the blameless Phaeacians brought here for him': ἔνεικαν is an aorist without the augment, and ἀμύμονες is the epithet whose sense is not really known, kept 'blameless'. δαιτί 'in the feast' is a dative. ἀοιδῆς ὕμνον 'the strain of song': ὕμνος here is a song or strain, not necessarily a hymn to a god.

sentences.t:
καί οἱ ἐγὼ τόδ’ ἄλεισον ἐμὸν περικαλλὲς ὀπάσσω,
χρύσεον, ὄφρ’ ἐμέθεν μεμνημένος ἤματα πάντα
σπένδῃ ἐνὶ μεγάρῳ Διί τ’ ἄλλοισίν τε θεοῖσιν.
sentences.tr:
kai hoi egō tod’ aleison emon perikalles opassō,
chryseon, ophr’ emethen memnēmenos ēmata panta
spendēi eni megarōi Dii t’ alloisin te theoisin.
sentences.l:
And to him I also this goblet of mine, very fair, will give,
golden, so that, of me mindful, all his days
he may pour libations in the hall to Zeus and to the other gods.”
sentences.i: And I too will give him this goblet of mine, a very fair one, of gold, so that, remembering me, he may pour libations in his hall to Zeus and the other gods for all his days.”
sentences.n: καί here is 'also, too'; οἱ 'to him'. ἄλεισον 'goblet' is a drinking-cup, a word of obscure origin. ἐμόν 'mine', περικαλλές 'very fair', χρύσεον 'golden' (uncontracted). ὀπάσσω 'I will give' (future of ὀπάζω, properly 'make follow, give besides'). ὄφρα ... σπένδῃ 'so that he may pour libations' is a subjunctive. ἐμέθεν 'of me' is the genitive (Attic ἐμοῦ) with μεμνημένος 'remembering'. ἤματα πάντα 'all his days' is an accusative of time. ἐνὶ μεγάρῳ 'in the hall'; Διί is the dative of Ζεύς; ἄλλοισίν τε θεοῖσιν 'and to the other gods'. The speech ends with this unit.

sentences.t:
ὣς ἔφατ’, Ἀρήτη δὲ μετὰ δμῳῇσιν ἔειπεν
ἀμφὶ πυρὶ στῆσαι τρίποδα μέγαν ὅττι τάχιστα.
sentences.tr:
hōs ephat’, Arētē de meta dmōiēisin eeipen
amphi pyri stēsai tripoda megan hotti tachista.
sentences.l:
So he spoke, and Arete among the maidservants spoke,
to set about the fire a great tripod as quickly as possible.
sentences.i: So he spoke, and Arete spoke among her maids, bidding them set a great tripod about the fire as quickly as possible.
sentences.n: ὣς ἔφατ’ 'So he spoke' (ἔφατο, elided). μετά ... ἔειπεν is a split verb (μετέειπεν 'spoke among'), with δμῳῇσιν, a dative plural in -ῃσιν, 'maidservants'. The infinitive στῆσαι 'to set up' (aorist of ἵστημι) carries the order. τρίποδα μέγαν 'a great tripod', a three-legged bronze cauldron. ὅττι τάχιστα 'as quickly as possible' (ὅττι is a doubled-τ form of ὅτι).

sentences.t:
αἱ δὲ λοετροχόον τρίποδ’ ἵστασαν ἐν πυρὶ κηλέῳ,
ἔν δ’ ἄρ’ ὕδωρ ἔχεαν, ὑπὸ δὲ ξύλα δαῖον ἑλοῦσαι.
sentences.tr:
hai de loetrochoon tripod’ histasan en pyri kēleōi,
en d’ ar’ hydōr echean, hypo de xyla daion helousai.
sentences.l:
And they the bath-water tripod set up on the blazing fire,
and water poured in, and beneath logs kindled, having taken them.
sentences.i: They set the bath-water tripod on the blazing fire, poured water into it, and took logs and kindled them beneath it.
sentences.n: αἱ δέ 'and they' (the article-form is a pronoun, feminine plural). λοετροχόον 'pouring bath-water' describes the tripod that heats water for a bath. ἵστασαν 'set up' (imperfect). κηλέῳ is a stock epithet of fire whose exact meaning is uncertain; the traditional gloss is 'blazing', which is kept. ἔν ... ἔχεαν is a split verb, 'poured in' (aorist of χέω, with the augment); ὑπὸ ... δαῖον is another, 'were kindling underneath'. ξύλα 'logs'; ἑλοῦσαι 'having taken' (aorist participle of αἱρέω, feminine plural).

sentences.t: γάστρην μὲν τρίποδος πῦρ ἄμφεπε, θέρμετο δ’ ὕδωρ·
sentences.tr: gastrēn men tripodos pyr amphepe, thermeto d’ hydōr·
sentences.l: The belly of the tripod indeed the fire was busy about, and the water grew warm;
sentences.i: The fire was busy about the belly of the tripod, and the water grew warm;
sentences.n: γάστρην μὲν τρίποδος 'the belly of the tripod', the bulging part of the vessel; μέν sets the fire against the water in the second half, marked by δέ. ἄμφεπε is an imperfect of ἀμφέπω 'be busy about, tend', without the augment. θέρμετο 'was growing warm' (imperfect passive of θέρμω).

sentences.t:
τόφρα δ’ ἄρ’ Ἀρήτη ξείνῳ περικαλλέα χηλὸν
ἐξέφερεν θαλάμοιο, τίθει δ’ ἐνὶ κάλλιμα δῶρα,
ἐσθῆτα χρυσόν τε, τά οἱ Φαίηκες ἔδωκαν·
sentences.tr:
tophra d’ ar’ Arētē xeinōi perikallea chēlon
exepheren thalamoio, tithei d’ eni kallima dōra,
esthēta chryson te, ta hoi Phaiēkes edōkan·
sentences.i: Meanwhile Arete brought out of the chamber a very fair chest for the stranger, and put fair gifts into it, clothing and gold, which the Phaeacians had given him;
sentences.n: τόφρα δέ 'and meanwhile', while the bath was heating. ξείνῳ 'for the stranger'. περικαλλέα χηλόν 'a very fair chest' (the same περικαλλής as at 420). ἐξέφερεν 'was bringing out' (imperfect); θαλάμοιο is a genitive of place-from-which, 'from the chamber', with the ending -οιο. τίθει 'she was putting' (imperfect, without the augment), with ἐνί 'in it' as an adverb. κάλλιμα 'fair' (from κάλλος, like περικαλλής). ἐσθῆτα 'clothing'; χρυσόν τε 'and gold'. τά οἱ Φαίηκες ἔδωκαν 'which the Phaeacians gave him'; ἔδωκαν is an aorist.

sentences.t:
ἐν δ’ αὐτὴ φᾶρος θῆκεν καλόν τε χιτῶνα,
καί μιν φωνήσασ’ ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα·
sentences.tr:
en d’ autē pharos thēken kalon te chitōna,
kai min phōnēsas’ epea pteroenta prosēuda·
sentences.l:
and in it herself she put a cloak and a fine tunic,
and, lifting her voice, to him winged words she spoke:
sentences.i: and she herself put in a cloak and a fine tunic, and, raising her voice, spoke winged words to him:
sentences.n: ἐν δ’ αὐτή 'and in it herself'. θῆκεν 'she put' (aorist of τίθημι). καλόν 'fine' stands between θῆκεν and χιτῶνα and is taken here with χιτῶνα, though it could also be heard with φᾶρος. The last line is the stock speech-opener with a feminine participle, φωνήσασ’ 'having lifted her voice', and it stands elsewhere word for word; its English is kept.

sentences.t:
αὐτὸς νῦν ἴδε πῶμα, θοῶς δ’ ἐπὶ δεσμὸν ἴηλον,
μή τίς τοι καθ’ ὁδὸν δηλήσεται, ὁππότ’ ἂν αὖτε
εὕδῃσθα γλυκὺν ὕπνον ἰὼν ἐν νηὶ μελαίνῃ.
sentences.tr:
autos nyn ide pōma, thoōs d’ epi desmon iēlon,
mē tis toi kath’ hodon dēlēsetai, hoppot’ an aute
heudēistha glykyn hypnon iōn en nēi melainēi.
sentences.l:
“Yourself now look to the lid, and swiftly upon it cast a fastening,
lest anyone on the way do you harm, whenever again
you sleep sweet sleep, going in a black ship.”
sentences.i: “See to the lid yourself now, and quickly put a fastening on it, so that no one may do you harm on the way, whenever you next sleep sweet sleep as you travel in a black ship.”
sentences.n: αὐτός 'yourself'. ἴδε is the aorist imperative of the verb 'see', here 'look to, see to'; πῶμα 'lid'. θοῶς 'swiftly'. ἐπὶ ... ἴηλον is a split verb, 'cast upon': ἴηλον is an imperative of ἰάλλω 'send, throw', and δεσμόν is 'a fastening, a knot'. μή τίς τοι ... δηλήσεται 'lest anyone harm you': μή 'lest', τοι 'you', and δηλήσεται a subjunctive of δηλέομαι 'do harm'. καθ’ ὁδόν 'on the way'. ὁππότ’ ἂν αὖτε εὕδῃσθα 'whenever again you sleep': εὕδῃσθα is a second-person subjunctive in the epic -σθα ending (Attic εὕδῃς). ἰών 'going' (participle of εἶμι). Arete speaks, so the quotation mark opens and the note above the line names her. The speech ends with this unit.

sentences.t:
αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ τό γ’ ἄκουσε πολύτλας δῖος Ὀδυσσεύς,
αὐτίκ’ ἐπήρτυε πῶμα, θοῶς δ’ ἐπὶ δεσμὸν ἴηλεν
ποικίλον, ὅν ποτέ μιν δέδαε φρεσὶ πότνια Κίρκη·
sentences.tr:
autar epei to g’ akouse polytlas dios Odysseus,
autik’ epērtye pōma, thoōs d’ epi desmon iēlen
poikilon, hon pote min dedae phresi potnia Kirkē·
sentences.i: But when much-enduring, heavenly Odysseus heard this, at once he fitted on the lid and quickly put on it an intricate fastening, which the lady Circe had once taught him in his mind.
sentences.n: αὐτὰρ ἐπεί 'but when'. τό γ’ 'this'. ἄκουσε 'he heard' (aorist without the augment). πολύτλας δῖος Ὀδυσσεύς 'much-enduring, heavenly Odysseus', two stock epithets, both kept every time. ἐπήρτυε 'fitted on, made ready' (imperfect of ἐπαρτύω). ἐπὶ ... ἴηλεν 'cast upon' is the indicative of the verb of 443. ποικίλον 'intricate' (ποικίλος is 'varied, many-patterned', and for a knot it is the twisting of the cord). ὅν is the relative 'which'; μιν 'him'; δέδαε 'taught' (a reduplicated aorist of δάω); φρεσί 'in his mind'. πότνια Κίρκη 'the lady Circe' (πότνια is 'lady, mistress').

sentences.t:
αὐτόδιον δ’ ἄρα μιν ταμίη λούσασθαι ἀνώγει
ἔς ῥ’ ἀσάμινθον βάνθ’·
sentences.tr:
autodion d’ ara min tamiē lousasthai anōgei
es rh’ asaminthon banth’·
sentences.l:
Straightway then him the housekeeper to bathe bade,
into the bath stepping;
sentences.i: At once the housekeeper bade him get into the bath and wash;
sentences.n: αὐτόδιον 'straightway, on the spot'. ταμίη 'the housekeeper'; λούσασθαι is an aorist middle infinitive, 'to wash himself, bathe'; ἀνώγει is an imperfect, 'bade'. ἔς ῥ’ ἀσάμινθον: ἔς is εἰς, ῥ’ is ῥα 'then', and ἀσάμινθον is 'bath' (accusative). βάνθ’ is the accusative participle βάντα 'having stepped', elided, agreeing with μιν 'him'.

sentences.t:
ὁ δ’ ἄρ ἀσπασίως ἴδε θυμῷ
θερμὰ λοέτρ’, ἐπεὶ οὔ τι κομιζόμενός γε θάμιζεν,
ἐπεὶ δὴ λίπε δῶμα Καλυψοῦς ἠυκόμοιο.
sentences.tr:
ho d’ ar aspasiōs ide thymōi
therma loetr’, epei ou ti komizomenos ge thamizen,
epei dē lipe dōma Kalypsous ēykomoio.
sentences.l:
And he gladly saw, in his heart,
the warm baths, since not at all being cared-for was he wont,
since now he had left the house of fine-haired Calypso.
sentences.i: and in his heart he saw the warm baths with joy, for he had not been in the way of being cared for ever since he left the house of fine-haired Calypso.
sentences.n: ὁ δ’ ἄρ: ὁ is the pronoun 'he'. ἀσπασίως 'gladly'; ἴδε 'he saw' (aorist, without the augment); θυμῷ 'in his heart' (a dative). θερμὰ λοέτρ’ 'the warm baths' (λοετρά, a neuter plural, elided). ἐπεὶ οὔ τι κομιζόμενός γε θάμιζεν 'since he was not in the habit of being cared for': κομιζόμενος 'being tended', and θάμιζεν 'he was accustomed, often was' (imperfect of θαμίζω). ἐπεὶ δὴ λίπε 'ever since he left' (λίπε, an aorist without the augment). Καλυψοῦς is the genitive of Καλυψώ. ἠυκόμοιο 'fine-haired' is a genitive in -οιο; ἠυ- is an epic variant of ἐυ-, printed without a diaeresis. Line 452 is metrically irregular as transmitted: its first syllable, the short ε of ἐπεί, has to be scanned long (metrical lengthening) to make a spondee of the first foot.

sentences.t: τόφρα δέ οἱ κομιδή γε θεῷ ὣς ἔμπεδος ἦεν.
sentences.tr: tophra de hoi komidē ge theōi hōs empedos ēen.
sentences.l: During that time for him care, indeed, as for a god, unfailing was.
sentences.i: But for that time the care he received was unfailing, as if he were a god.
sentences.n: τόφρα 'for that time', looking back to the time in Calypso's house named in the line before. κομιδή 'care, tending' is the subject; οἱ 'for him'; γε 'indeed'. θεῷ ὣς 'as for a god': ὥς 'as' is accented here because it comes after its word. ἔμπεδος 'steady, unfailing'; ἦεν is the epic imperfect of εἰμί 'be'.

sentences.t:
τὸν δ’ ἐπεὶ οὖν δμῳαὶ λοῦσαν καὶ χρῖσαν ἐλαίῳ,
ἀμφὶ δέ μιν χλαῖναν καλὴν βάλον ἠδὲ χιτῶνα,
ἔκ ῥ’ ἀσαμίνθου βὰς ἄνδρας μέτα οἰνοποτῆρας
ἤιε·
sentences.tr:
ton d’ epei oun dmōiai lousan kai chrisan elaiōi,
amphi de min chlainan kalēn balon ēde chitōna,
ek rh’ asaminthou bas andras meta oinopotēras
ēie·
sentences.l:
And him when then the maidservants had washed and anointed with oil,
and about him a fine cloak had thrown and a tunic,
out of the bath stepping, among the men, the wine-drinkers,
he went;
sentences.i: And when the maids had washed him and anointed him with oil, and had thrown a fine cloak and a tunic about him, he stepped out of the bath and went among the wine-drinking men;
sentences.n: τὸν δ’: τὸν is the pronoun 'him'. ἐπεὶ οὖν 'when then'. δμῳαί 'maidservants' (nominative plural). λοῦσαν 'washed' and χρῖσαν 'anointed' are aorists without the augment (λούω, χρίω); ἐλαίῳ 'with oil'. ἀμφὶ ... βάλον is a split verb, 'threw about'. χλαῖναν 'a cloak', here the heavier outer garment; ἠδὲ χιτῶνα 'and a tunic'. ἔκ ῥ’ ἀσαμίνθου βάς 'stepping out of the bath' (βάς is an aorist participle of βαίνω). ἄνδρας μέτα οἰνοποτῆρας 'among the wine-drinking men': μέτα stands after its noun. ἤιε 'he went' is the epic imperfect of εἶμι.

sentences.t:
Ναυσικάα δὲ θεῶν ἄπο κάλλος ἔχουσα
στῆ ῥα παρὰ σταθμὸν τέγεος πύκα ποιητοῖο,
θαύμαζεν δ’ Ὀδυσῆα ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖσιν ὁρῶσα,
καί μιν φωνήσασ’ ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα·
sentences.tr:
Nausikaa de theōn apo kallos echousa
stē rha para stathmon tegeos pyka poiētoio,
thaumazen d’ Odysēa en ophthalmoisin horōsa,
kai min phōnēsas’ epea pteroenta prosēuda·
sentences.l:
and Nausicaa, from the gods beauty having,
stood then beside the doorpost of the close-built roof,
and marvelled at Odysseus, with her eyes looking,
and, lifting her voice, to him winged words she spoke:
sentences.i: and Nausicaa, who had her beauty from the gods, stood by the doorpost of the well-built hall, and marvelled at Odysseus as she looked at him with her eyes, and, raising her voice, spoke winged words to him:
sentences.n: θεῶν ἄπο κάλλος ἔχουσα 'having beauty from the gods': ἄπο stands after its noun. στῆ 'she stood' (aorist of ἵστημι, without the augment); ῥα 'then'. σταθμόν 'doorpost'. τέγεος πύκα ποιητοῖο 'of the close-built roof' (the roofed hall); this line stands elsewhere word for word, and its English is kept. θαύμαζεν 'she was marvelling' (imperfect). Ὀδυσῆα is the accusative in the Ionic spelling (also Ὀδυσσῆα). ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖσιν ὁρῶσα 'looking with her eyes'. The last line is the stock speech-opener with a feminine participle, and it too stands elsewhere unchanged.

sentences.t:
χαῖρε, ξεῖν’, ἵνα καί ποτ’ ἐὼν ἐν πατρίδι γαίῃ
μνήσῃ ἐμεῦ, ὅτι μοι πρώτῃ ζωάγρι’ ὀφέλλεις.
sentences.tr:
chaire, xein’, hina kai pot’ eōn en patridi gaiēi
mnēsēi emeu, hoti moi prōtēi zōagri’ ophelleis.
sentences.l:
“Welcome, stranger, so that even someday, being in your fatherland,
you may remember me, because to me first the life-price you owe.”
sentences.i: “Welcome, stranger, so that some day, in your fatherland, you may remember me, for it is to me first that you owe the price of your life.”
sentences.n: χαῖρε, ξεῖν’ 'Welcome, stranger' (ξεῖν’ is ξεῖνε elided). ἵνα 'so that' takes the subjunctive μνήσῃ 'you may remember', with ἐμεῦ 'me' (the Ionic genitive, Attic ἐμοῦ). καί ποτε 'even some day'. ἐών is the Ionic participle 'being' (Attic ὤν); ἐν πατρίδι γαίῃ 'in your fatherland', with an Ionic dative in -ῃ. ὅτι 'because'; μοι πρώτῃ 'to me first'. ζωάγρια is a rare word, a compound built on ζωός 'alive' with the sense 'payment due for saving a life'; ὀφέλλεις 'you owe'. Nausicaa begins to speak here, so the quotation mark opens and the note above the line names her; her speech ends with this unit.

sentences.t: τὴν δ’ ἀπαμειβόμενος προσέφη πολύμητις Ὀδυσσεύς.
sentences.tr: tēn d’ apameibomenos prosephē polymētis Odysseus.
sentences.l: Her answering addressed many-wiled Odysseus:
sentences.i: In answer Odysseus of many wiles said to her:
sentences.n: The reply-formula with a feminine pronoun: τὴν 'her', ἀπαμειβόμενος 'answering', προσέφη 'addressed', πολύμητις 'of many wiles'. The archive prints a full stop at the end of this line where the same line at 412 has a raised dot; the English colon still marks a speech to come. The line stands unchanged elsewhere, and its English is kept.

sentences.t:
Ναυσικάα θύγατερ μεγαλήτορος Ἀλκινόοιο,
οὕτω νῦν Ζεὺς θείη, ἐρίγδουπος πόσις Ἥρης,
οἴκαδέ τ’ ἐλθέμεναι καὶ νόστιμον ἦμαρ ἰδέσθαι·
sentences.tr:
Nausikaa thygater megalētoros Alkinooio,
houtō nyn Zeus theiē, erigdoupos posis Hērēs,
oikade t’ elthemenai kai nostimon ēmar idesthai·
sentences.i: “Nausicaa, daughter of great-spirited Alcinous, so may Zeus now ordain, loud-crashing husband of Hera, that I come home and see the day of my homecoming;
sentences.n: Ναυσικάα and θύγατερ are vocatives. μεγαλήτορος is the genitive of μεγαλήτωρ 'great-spirited', a stock epithet; Ἀλκινόοιο is a genitive in -οιο. οὕτω νῦν Ζεὺς θείη 'so now may Zeus ordain': θείη is an aorist optative of τίθημι 'set, appoint', and the two infinitives that follow are what he is asked to ordain. ἐρίγδουπος 'loud-crashing' is built on an intensifying prefix and δοῦπος 'a heavy sound, a crash'; the traditional gloss is thunder. πόσις 'husband'; Ἥρης is the Ionic genitive of Ἥρη. οἴκαδε 'homewards' (οἶκον with the direction-suffix -δε); ἐλθέμεναι is an infinitive in -έμεναι, and ἰδέσθαι an aorist middle infinitive. The whole line οἴκαδέ τ’ ἐλθέμεναι καὶ νόστιμον ἦμαρ ἰδέσθαι stands elsewhere word for word, and its English is kept. Odysseus answers here, so the quotation mark opens and the note above the line names him.

sentences.t:
τῷ κέν τοι καὶ κεῖθι θεῷ ὣς εὐχετοῴμην
αἰεὶ ἤματα πάντα·
sentences.tr:
tōi ken toi kai keithi theōi hōs euchetoōimēn
aiei ēmata panta·
sentences.l:
then to you, even there, as to a god, I would pray
always, all my days;
sentences.i: then even there I would pray to you as to a god, always, for all my days;
sentences.n: τῷ 'then, in that case' (a dative used as an adverb). κέν is κε(ν) 'would'; τοι 'to you'; καὶ κεῖθι 'even there', that is in his own country. θεῷ ὣς 'as to a god'. εὐχετοῴμην is an optative of εὐχετάομαι 'pray to' in its uncontracted -όω- shape, with κέν: 'I would pray'. αἰεί 'always'; ἤματα πάντα 'all my days' is an accusative of time.

sentences.t: σὺ γάρ μ’ ἐβιώσαο, κούρη.
sentences.tr: sy gar m’ ebiōsao, kourē.
sentences.l: for you gave me life, maiden.”
sentences.i: for it is you who gave me life, maiden.”
sentences.n: σὺ γάρ 'for you'; μ’ is με 'me'. ἐβιώσαο is a second-person aorist middle of βιόω, with the epic ending -αο (Attic -ω), 'you gave me life, brought me back to life'; it is the reason for the prayer. κούρη 'maiden' is a vocative. The speech ends with this unit.

sentences.t: ἦ ῥα καὶ ἐς θρόνον ἷζε παρ’ Ἀλκίνοον βασιλῆα·
sentences.tr: ē rha kai es thronon hize par’ Alkinoon basilēa·
sentences.l: He spoke, and to a chair he sat down, beside Alcinous the king;
sentences.i: So he said, and sat down in a chair beside King Alcinous;
sentences.n: ἦ ῥα καί closes a speech, as at 416. ἐς θρόνον ἷζε 'he sat down on a chair': ἷζε is an imperfect of ἵζω. παρ’ Ἀλκίνοον βασιλῆα 'beside Alcinous the king': παρά with the accusative gives 'to the side of'.

sentences.t: οἱ δ’ ἤδη μοίρας τ’ ἔνεμον κερόωντό τε οἶνον.
sentences.tr: hoi d’ ēdē moiras t’ enemon keroōnto te oinon.
sentences.l: And they now portions were dividing and were mixing the wine.
sentences.i: By now they were dividing the portions and mixing the wine.
sentences.n: οἱ δ’ 'and they' (a pronoun, the other feasters). μοίρας here are shares of the meat, 'portions', not fate. ἔνεμον 'were distributing' (imperfect of νέμω). κερόωντο is an imperfect middle of κεράννυμι 'mix', in the uncontracted epic shape: they were mixing the wine for themselves.

sentences.t:
κῆρυξ δ’ ἐγγύθεν ἦλθεν ἄγων ἐρίηρον ἀοιδόν,
Δημόδοκον λαοῖσι τετιμένον·
sentences.tr:
kēryx d’ engythen ēlthen agōn eriēron aoidon,
Dēmodokon laoisi tetimenon·
sentences.l:
And the herald from close by came, leading the trusty minstrel,
Demodocus, honoured by the people;
sentences.i: The herald came from close by, leading the trusty minstrel, Demodocus, who was held in honour by the people;
sentences.n: ἐγγύθεν 'from close by' (-θεν marks the place from which). ἦλθεν 'came' (aorist); ἄγων 'leading'. ἐρίηρον 'trusty' is the stock epithet of the minstrel, with the traditional gloss 'trusty'; ἀοιδός is 'minstrel', and Δημόδοκον stands beside it. λαοῖσι τετιμένον 'held in honour by the people': λαοῖσι is a dative plural in -οισι, and τετιμένον is a perfect passive participle of τιμάω. The first line of this unit stands elsewhere word for word, and its English is kept.

sentences.t:
εἷσε δ’ ἄρ’ αὐτὸν
μέσσῳ δαιτυμόνων, πρὸς κίονα μακρὸν ἐρείσας.
sentences.tr:
heise d’ ar’ auton
messōi daitymonōn, pros kiona makron ereisas.
sentences.l:
and he seated him
in the middle of the feasters, having propped him against a tall pillar.
sentences.i: and he seated him in the middle of the feasters, propping him against a tall pillar.
sentences.n: εἷσε 'he seated' (aorist of ἵζω in its causative sense). αὐτόν 'him'. μέσσῳ δαιτυμόνων 'in the middle of the feasters': μέσσῳ is a dative with the doubled σ, and δαιτυμόνων a genitive plural. πρὸς κίονα μακρόν 'against a tall pillar'. ἐρείσας 'having propped' (aorist participle of ἐρείδω) has no object of its own; the same words close a line elsewhere where a chair is the thing propped, but here the natural reading is the minstrel himself, and the English says 'him'.

sentences.t:
δὴ τότε κήρυκα προσέφη πολύμητις Ὀδυσσεύς,
νώτου ἀποπροταμών, ἐπὶ δὲ πλεῖον ἐλέλειπτο,
ἀργιόδοντος ὑός, θαλερὴ δ’ ἦν ἀμφὶς ἀλοιφή·
sentences.tr:
dē tote kēryka prosephē polymētis Odysseus,
nōtou apoprotamōn, epi de pleion eleleipto,
argiodontos hyos, thalerē d’ ēn amphis aloiphē·
sentences.i: Then Odysseus of many wiles said to the herald, cutting a piece from the chine of a white-toothed pig, of which more remained over, while the fat on both sides was abundant:
sentences.n: δὴ τότε 'then indeed'. κήρυκα 'the herald' is the accusative object of προσέφη 'addressed'. πολύμητις Ὀδυσσεύς 'Odysseus of many wiles'. νώτου ἀποπροταμών 'cutting off from the chine': ἀποπροταμών is an aorist participle, and νώτου is a genitive of the part, the back-cut. ἐπὶ δὲ πλεῖον ἐλέλειπτο 'and more was left over': ἐπί is an adverb, and ἐλέλειπτο is a pluperfect passive of λείπω. ἀργιόδοντος ὑός 'of a white-toothed pig' (ὑός is the genitive of ὗς). θαλερή, from a root meaning 'bloom, thrive', is 'abundant' here. ἀμφίς 'on both sides'; ἀλοιφή 'fat'. His speech follows in the next unit.

sentences.t:
κῆρυξ, τῆ δή, τοῦτο πόρε κρέας, ὄφρα φάγῃσιν,
Δημοδόκῳ·
sentences.tr:
kēryx, tē dē, touto pore kreas, ophra phagēisin,
Dēmodokōi·
sentences.l:
“Herald, here, this meat give, that he may eat,
to Demodocus;
sentences.i: “Herald, here, take this meat and give it to Demodocus, so that he may eat;
sentences.n: κῆρυξ is a vocative. τῆ δή is an exclamation that goes with an offered thing, 'here, take this'. πόρε is an aorist imperative, 'give'. τοῦτο κρέας 'this meat'. ὄφρα φάγῃσιν 'so that he may eat': φάγῃσιν is a subjunctive with the ending -σιν. Δημοδόκῳ 'to Demodocus' (dative). Odysseus begins to speak to the herald here, so the quotation mark opens and the note above the line names him.

sentences.t: καί μιν προσπτύξομαι ἀχνύμενός περ·
sentences.tr: kai min prosptyxomai achnymenos per·
sentences.l: and I will greet him, grieving though I am;
sentences.i: and I will greet him, grieving though I am;
sentences.n: προσπτύξομαι is a future middle, 'I will greet, embrace with a greeting'. ἀχνύμενος 'grieving'; περ 'though', a particle that makes the participle concessive.

sentences.t:
πᾶσι γὰρ ἀνθρώποισιν ἐπιχθονίοισιν ἀοιδοὶ
τιμῆς ἔμμοροί εἰσι καὶ αἰδοῦς, οὕνεκ’ ἄρα σφέας
οἴμας μοῦσ’ ἐδίδαξε, φίλησε δὲ φῦλον ἀοιδῶν.
sentences.tr:
pasi gar anthrōpoisin epichthonioisin aoidoi
timēs emmoroi eisi kai aidous, hounek’ ara spheas
oimas mous’ edidaxe, philēse de phylon aoidōn.
sentences.l:
For among all men upon the earth minstrels
of honour have a share and of reverence, because them
the lays the Muse taught, and she loved the tribe of minstrels.”
sentences.i: For among all men who live on the earth minstrels have their share of honour and reverence, because the Muse taught them the lays and loved the tribe of minstrels.”
sentences.n: πᾶσι ... ἀνθρώποισιν ἐπιχθονίοισιν 'among all men upon the earth': the datives are in -οισιν, and ἐπιχθόνιος is 'upon the earth'. ἀοιδοί 'minstrels'. τιμῆς ἔμμοροί εἰσι καὶ αἰδοῦς 'have a share in honour and reverence': ἔμμορος takes a genitive. οὕνεκα 'because'; σφέας is the Ionic accusative plural 'them'. οἴμας 'lays' is an accusative plural of οἴμη 'strain of song', a word often tied to οἶμος 'path', so 'the paths of song' is also heard. ἐδίδαξε 'taught' (aorist, with the augment); φίλησε 'loved' (aorist, without it). μοῦσα 'the Muse'; φῦλον ἀοιδῶν 'the tribe of minstrels'. The speech ends with this unit.

sentences.t:
ὣς ἄρ’ ἔφη, κῆρυξ δὲ φέρων ἐν χερσὶν ἔθηκεν
ἥρῳ Δημοδόκῳ·
sentences.tr:
hōs ar’ ephē, kēryx de pherōn en chersin ethēken
hērōi Dēmodokōi·
sentences.l:
So he spoke, and the herald, carrying it, in his hands placed it
for the hero Demodocus;
sentences.i: So he spoke, and the herald took it and put it into the hands of the hero Demodocus;
sentences.n: ὣς ἄρ’ ἔφη 'so he spoke'. φέρων 'carrying'; ἐν χερσὶν ἔθηκεν 'he placed in his hands'. ἥρῳ is the dative of ἥρως, an honorific title for a man of standing, 'hero', kept as 'the hero' every time.

sentences.t: ὁ δ’ ἐδέξατο, χαῖρε δὲ θυμῷ.
sentences.tr: ho d’ edexato, chaire de thymōi.
sentences.l: and he received it, and rejoiced in his heart.
sentences.i: and he received it and was glad in his heart.
sentences.n: ὁ 'he' is a pronoun. ἐδέξατο 'received' (aorist of δέχομαι). χαῖρε here is a past tense, 'he rejoiced', not the greeting 'welcome' of the imperatives above; the form is the same, and only the sense of the sentence tells them apart. θυμῷ 'in his heart'.

sentences.t: οἱ δ’ ἐπ’ ὀνείαθ’ ἑτοῖμα προκείμενα χεῖρας ἴαλλον.
sentences.tr: hoi d’ ep’ oneiath’ hetoima prokeimena cheiras iallon.
sentences.l: And they to the good things ready and set before them put out their hands.
sentences.i: And they put out their hands to the good things lying ready before them.
sentences.n: ὀνείαθ’ 'good things, provisions' is a neuter plural, elided; ἑτοῖμα 'ready' and προκείμενα 'lying before them' agree with it. ἐπ’ ... ἴαλλον is a split verb, 'were sending forth (their hands) to', an imperfect of ἰάλλω. The line stands elsewhere word for word, and its English is kept.

sentences.t:
αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ πόσιος καὶ ἐδητύος ἐξ ἔρον ἕντο,
δὴ τότε Δημόδοκον προσέφη πολύμητις Ὀδυσσεύς·
sentences.tr:
autar epei posios kai edētyos ex eron hento,
dē tote Dēmodokon prosephē polymētis Odysseus·
sentences.l:
But when of drink and of food they had put away desire,
then indeed to Demodocus addressed many-wiled Odysseus:
sentences.i: But when they had put from them the desire for drink and food, then Odysseus of many wiles said to Demodocus:
sentences.n: αὐτὰρ ἐπεί 'but when'. πόσιος καὶ ἐδητύος 'of drink and of food' are genitives that depend on ἔρον 'desire', and ἐξ ... ἕντο is a split verb, 'sent out from themselves' (aorist middle of ἵημι), the stock way to close a meal. δὴ τότε 'then indeed'; Δημόδοκον is the accusative object of προσέφη 'addressed'. Odysseus' speech to the minstrel runs on into the next part, so no quotation mark is opened here.
